newsitem.title: NORWAY: NYCOMED SHARES JUMP ON H1 RESULT.
newsitem.headline: NYCOMED SHARES JUMP ON H1 RESULT.

text.p: Shares in Norwegian drugs company Nycomed ASA rose sharply on Thursday following the release of better-than-expected first-half 1997 profits.
At 0935 GMT, Nycomed A class shares were up 3.73 percent at 167 crowns and the B share had increased 4.39 percent to 155 crowns in relatively high turnover on the Oslo stock exchange.

Nycomed, which plans to merge with Britain's Amersham International Plc soon, posted profits of 604 million crowns. The result fell 74 million crowns short of the corresponding 1996 pre-tax profit, but it beat market expectations.

"The result was better than expected in several divisions," an Oslo dealer said. "Imaging did very well. Things look good in the United States. Nycomed has not lost as many market shares there as you might have expected. This was a positive result and it increases the chances for the merger to come through."

"There is also a rumour that the new company, Nycomed Amersham, will become big enough to be listed on the FTSE. Many investors will want to increase their stake in the company then," the dealer said.
